title: Introduce probe-autotuner and causal-attribution fence for performance canaries
author: Ananya Rao
description:
Motivation: our continuous perf canary system shows false-positive regressions during traffic shape shifts and under low-signal cohorts. This PR adds two coordinated components to reduce spurious rollbacks and improve diagnosis: 1) a Probe Autotuner that dynamically adapts synthetic probe frequency and traffic slicing based on observed SLO budget consumption and signal-to-noise ratio, and 2) a Causal Attribution Fence that uses cohort-based weighting and lightweight instrumental-variable style checks to deconfound throughput/latency signals from traffic composition changes.

What this changes (high-level): - New service: canary/supervisor/probe_autotuner.go + controller for dynamic probe scheduling. - New analysis pipeline: canary/attribution/causal_fence.go that annotates canary reports with attribution confidence and recommends guarded actions (quarantine, partial rollback, continue). - Rollout guard policy changes: Policy engine gains a new `attribution_score` input; the canary orchestration now consults the causal fence and requires quorum from multiple signal families before triggering full rollback. - Telemetry: Prometheus metrics and tracing spans added for autotuner decisions, attribution latency, and cohort weights; new Grafana panels in observability/dashboards/canary_attribution.json. - E2E test harness: perf-canary/harness/replica_simulator_test.go extended with traffic-shape perturbations and golden expectations.

Design notes: Probe Autotuner: the autotuner monitors per-cohort effective sample size (ESS) and SLO budget spend-rate; when ESS drops below threshold it increases probe intensity for underrepresented cohorts while lowering synthetic probes for stable cohorts. It uses an exponentially-weighted frontier estimator to keep probe cost bounded and provide target confidence windows for latency percentiles used by detectors. Causal Attribution Fence: the fence computes cohort-conditioned deltas and then runs a lightweight permutation-based check plus a traffic-instrument score (traffic feature that is orthogonal to server-side resources) to estimate the chance that observed latency deltas are driven by traffic composition. A high attribution_score means the regression is likely caused by a model/infra change; a low score suggests traffic skew and triggers conservative actions (shadowed rollback, quenched alerting).

Compatibility and rollout: default behavior is opt-in per workspace via canary policy config (canary.policy.v2.use_causal_fence = false). For Redwood-managed tenants we will gradually enable the autotuner in a staged rollout: 10% of accounts -> 50% -> 100% over three weeks. The PR also ships a migration job to populate historical cohort boundaries for tenants that opt in.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation of autotuner and fence - [x] Unit tests for core heuristics - [x] Integration tests with replica_simulator - [x] Prometheus metrics + dashboard panels - [x] Docs section (observability docs) - [x] Linear links and rollout plan attached

Related: Linear ENG-1284 (reduce false-positive rollbacks), ENG-1290 (dynamic probe scheduling).

release_notes: Add probe autotuner (dynamic probe scheduling) and causal attribution fence to reduce false-positive canary rollbacks during traffic shifts. Opt-in by default; rollout schedule included. Metrics and dashboards added.
notes_for_ops: When enabling for a tenant, monitor canary_probe_cost_total and attribution_confidence buckets for the first 48 hours. If probe_cost spikes > 2x baseline, rollback autotuner for that workspace. Ops runbook: run `tools/canary/validate_cohort_bounds` before enabling to ensure historical cohorts are populated.
additional_context: This PR is driven by recurring incidents where high tail latency correlated with ad-hoc traffic spikes in early-morning batches (see incident INT-3342). The attribution fence is intentionally conservative: it favors quarantine/partial rollback when uncertainty is high rather than full rollback, allowing platform teams to investigate without widespread customer impact. The algorithm intentionally integrates with the existing canary registry so past canary decisions remain auditable.
human_readable_summary: Adds an autotuner to adapt probe intensity across cohorts and a causal-fence analyzer to deconfound traffic-driven noise from true regressions; improves canary decision quality and reduces noisy rollbacks.
